who: Historian of religion in Latin America at Florida International University, PhD Catholic University of Louvain.

evidence.says: Sandra Milena Londono-Ardila's 2022 FIU dissertation, Vanguards of Liberation, identifies Ana Maria Bidegain as co-major professor.
FIU's faculty biography describes Bidegain's Louvain doctorate, research on religion in Latin American history, and earlier teaching at Universidad Nacional de Colombia and Universidad de los Andes.
The candidate authority connects Ana María Bidegaín, Bidegaín de Urán, and Bidegain Greising; its source notes identify a Latin American history professor at the same two Colombian universities.

notes: The dissertation confirms supervision directly; the authority's name variants and earlier affiliations connect the candidate to the FIU professor.

who: Historian of modern Chinese intellectual and political thought at Ohio State University, 1968–1998, PhD Harvard 1966.

evidence.says: Ohio State's MCLC Resource Center records Chang's Harvard doctorate in 1966, Chinese intellectual-history specialization, and Ohio State teaching from 1968 to 1998.
The candidate authority's note for Liang Chʻi-chʻao and intellectual transition in China identifies Chang Hao as a Harvard PhD and associate professor of history at Ohio State.

notes: Candidate and supervisor share the institution, period, and specialization; 1995 falls within the documented Ohio State appointment.

who: Steven K. Ross, historian of ancient Rome at Louisiana State University, PhD Berkeley 1997.

evidence.says: John J. Poirot's 2014 history dissertation on Romano-Parthian relations and Tacitus lists Steven K. Ross as committee chair.
LSU identifies Ross as a historian of Rome and the Near East, with a Berkeley PhD in 1997 and the book Roman Edessa.
Candidate p-67759 is Steven Joseph/J. Ross, author of Workers on the Edge and Working-Class Hollywood, a Princeton PhD and USC history professor.
Candidate p-126604 is Steven T. Ross, a Princeton PhD associated with the Naval War College and works on military and diplomatic history.

notes: Neither candidate is LSU's Steven K. Ross; both have different doctoral institutions and fields.

who: Foster Todd Smith, historian of Native America and the Texas borderlands at the University of North Texas, PhD Tulane 1989.

evidence.says: Bradley Folsom's August 2014 UNT dissertation on Joaquín de Arredondo names Smith, F. Todd (Foster Todd), as major professor.
F. Todd Smith received his Tulane US-history PhD in 1989, joined UNT in 1997, and wrote The Caddo Indians and other books on Texas Indians.
The candidate authority expands F. Todd to Foster Todd, identifies The Caddo Indians, and records a Tulane doctorate in 1989.

notes: The dissertation supplies the candidate's full name directly. The Franklin Smith candidate is unnecessary to the match.

who: William Phillips, history professor at Arizona State University during the 1980s.

evidence.says: ASU's 1985/86 speakers list identifies William Phillips in History, including the topics of teaching history and presidential assassinations.
A state employee publication describes William Phillips as having retired after 32 years in ASU's History Department and announcing a lecture on Ben Daniels and Theodore Roosevelt.
The supplied candidate authority is William D. Phillips, Jr., author of Enrique IV and A Concise History of Spain.
Cambridge identifies William D. Phillips, Jr. as a University of Minnesota history professor whose works concern Spain, Columbus, and slavery.

notes: The long-serving ASU professor and the Minnesota historian of Spain have distinct institutional careers and works.

who: James Cooper, Jr., historian of colonial New England at Oklahoma State University, PhD University of Connecticut.

evidence.says: The 2002–03 graduate faculty list identifies James Cooper, Jr. as associate professor of history with BA, MA, and PhD degrees from Connecticut.
OSU reports that history professor James Cooper helped authenticate colonial church records in Massachusetts.
The candidate is James Fenimore Cooper, the author catalogued for The Prairie (1827), The Pioneers, and The Last of the Mohicans.

notes: The candidate is the nineteenth-century novelist, a different person from the modern Oklahoma State historian.

who: Thomas Kelly, historian of ancient Greece and professor emeritus of history at the University of Minnesota, author of A History of Argos to 500 B.C.

evidence.says: The university press identifies the author Thomas Kelly as Minnesota professor emeritus of history and describes his study of ancient Argos.
Candidate T. Mills Kelly is a George Mason historian of digital public history and modern East Central Europe, with a George Washington University PhD in 1996.
The Thomas Kelly authority concerns an adult-education scholar and author on the history of British public libraries.
The ORCID candidate lists a Berkeley political-science PhD, an independent-scholar affiliation, and works on contemporary public policy and research methods.

notes: The three candidates have different fields and career identities from Minnesota's ancient Greek historian.

who: Romeyn Taylor, professor of Chinese history at the University of Minnesota, 1960–1994, PhD Chicago 1960.

evidence.says: The obituary records Taylor's Chinese-history professorship at Minnesota from 1960 to 1994 and his Chicago PhD in 1960.
The candidate is R. E. (Royal Ervin) Taylor, associated with the anthropology department at the University of California, Riverside and Advances in Obsidian Glass Studies.

notes: Romeyn Taylor and Royal Ervin Taylor have different names, institutions, and specializations.
